item.title: Seventy Percent Says the Fed Hikes in December — Oct 30, 2026 · 5:10 PM ET
item.description:
Seventy Percent Says the Fed Hikes in December

The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% on October 28, but it was not a quiet hold. The vote was 10-2, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack both voting for a quarter-point hike right away. Prediction markets read the dissents as a forwarding address: the hike the committee skipped in October is now priced to arrive in December.

As of October 30 at 5:00 PM ET, Kalshi prices a 25-point hike on December 9 at 69%, a hold at 28%, a 50-point hike at about 3% and a cut at 1% — a 72% chance of a hike in total. Polymarket prices the same 25-point hike at 70.5%, and fed funds futures are higher still at 73.3%. DeFi Rate's last trades tell the same story: Kalshi at 68.5 cents with $60K traded in 24 hours, Polymarket at 70.5 cents with $173K traded.

The crowd has earned some trust here. The market favorite has won 15 of 15 Fed decisions since 2025 on Kalshi and Polymarket, and October was graded close: Polymarket closed the hold at 95.5% and Kalshi at 94.5%. December's hike odds first closed above 50% on August 15 and sit at 73% on the latest daily close, even after slipping 3 points this week from 72% to 69% on Kalshi's decision contract.

Beyond December, the path goes quiet. January 27 prices a hike at just 26% to 28% against a 71% hold, and March is a coin flip at 50% hike, 47% hold. Kalshi's dot-plot ladder, which prices the Fed's own year-end 2026 projection, implies a median dot of 4.00% to 4.10% — exactly one more hike, delivered in December and then a pause.

What moves it next is data, starting with payrolls on November 6. The statement lands at 2:00 PM ET on December 9 with a new dot plot attached. Until then, every inflation print is a trade: hot, and 70% becomes 80%; soft, and the two dissenters start to look early rather than right.

item.title: Five Minutes at a Time — Oct 30, 2026 · 4:17 PM ET
item.description:
Five Minutes at a Time

Prediction markets used to ask where Bitcoin would close the month. Now they ask where it closes in the next five minutes.

On October 28, Polymarket's regulated U.S. platform launched five-minute up-or-down contracts on Bitcoin, Ether, Solana and XRP. Each contract asks one question: does the price finish the five-minute window above or below where it started? A correct call pays $1 a share; a wrong one pays nothing. With 288 windows a day per asset, the platform now runs crypto contracts at five-minute, 15-minute, hourly, daily, weekly and monthly intervals.

The format is proven. Polymarket's international platform introduced five-minute crypto contracts in February and generated roughly $4 billion in volume in their first six months. The U.S. versions run through QCX LLC under CFTC oversight and settle against CF Benchmarks pricing using time-weighted averages, a safeguard added in August.

The launch lands under a microscope: the CFTC is reviewing Polymarket's compliance with its 2022 settlement even as the contracts go live. Speed is the product now, and the scrutiny scales with it.

Sources: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/29/polymarket-brings-ultra-short-crypto-prediction-markets-to-u-s-platform

The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays on October 28 to win the 2026 World Series. On Kalshi, the series was also one of the biggest trading events of the year.

The 2027 market opened immediately. The Dodgers lead at 22.7%, the champion Brewers sit second at 11.9%, and the Yankees are third at 11%.

item.title: Coinbase's $200 Million Side Door — Oct 30, 2026 · 4:17 PM ET
item.description:
Coinbase's $200 Million Side Door

Coinbase's fastest-growing product is not crypto trading. It is prediction markets.

Reporting third-quarter results on October 29, Coinbase said its prediction markets business passed $200 million in annualized revenue, up from more than $100 million in the second quarter. Revenue from the product has compounded at 82% per quarter since launch, daily traders rose more than 60% in the quarter, and CEO Brian Armstrong called it one of the fastest-growing products by revenue in Coinbase history.

The detail that matters: more than half the contracts traded in Q3 were non-sports. Prediction markets are pulling in users who then trade crypto — Coinbase says prediction traders drive incremental spot volume — and the revenue is, in CFO Alesia Haas's words, less correlated to crypto volatility.

Next comes vertical integration. The CFTC cleared Coinbase Clearing LLC as a derivatives clearing organization on September 28, and Armstrong told investors Coinbase can now list its own prediction contracts instead of only routing flow to partners. In a slow crypto quarter, the side door is becoming a main entrance.

item.title: Google Now Answers Election Questions With a Market — Oct 30, 2026 · 4:17 PM ET
item.description:
Google Now Answers Election Questions With a Market

Ask Google for an election forecast this fall, and there is a coin flip's chance the answer comes from a betting market.

A CasinoReviews.net study of 140 Google results pages across 14 U.S. cities found Polymarket or Kalshi on page one for half of everyday forecast searches like 'election forecast' and 'midterm polls.' Kalshi appeared on all 28 pages sampled for 'senate odds' and 'midterm odds.' Almost nobody is searching for odds — about 1 in 120 midterm searches uses betting language — yet for half of the rest, Google surfaces a market anyway.

The sharpest finding: the platforms appeared in all eight cities tested in states where election betting is banned. Twenty-four states prohibit it outright, while federally regulated exchanges offer election contracts nationwide — a conflict now being argued in court.

The polls are no longer the forecast of record. The market is — whether the searcher asked for it or not.

The $65 Billion Month

October was the biggest month prediction markets have ever had — and it was not close.

Kalshi traded approximately $65 billion in October, 10% above its September record. Polymarket US reached $10 billion, up roughly 15% on its previous high. Open interest set records on both platforms: $2.05 billion on Kalshi and $384 million on Polymarket US. A year ago, Kalshi's entire October was about $4.4 billion.

The structure of the market flipped with the scale. Kalshi now accounts for nearly 83% of combined volume across itself and both Polymarket platforms, and U.S.-regulated venues hold 95.6% of the total. The offshore upstart era is over; the volume lives on regulated American exchanges now.

The test comes next week. The midterms end Tuesday, and post-election volume will show whether October was a peak or a plateau — whether $65 billion months are the new baseline or an election-season spike.

item.description:
Fifteen Percent Is the Favorite: The Super Bowl Market Has No Front-Runner

Super Bowl LXI is on February 14, 2027 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, and the prediction markets cannot find a favorite. The San Francisco 49ers lead the board at about 15% on DeFi Rate's cross-exchange average — 15.5 cents on Kalshi, 14.1 cents on Polymarket. A 15% favorite means the market thinks someone else wins about 85% of the time.

The chase pack is tight. The Buffalo Bills sit second at 12% — 11.5 cents on Kalshi, 12 cents on Polymarket — and the Kansas City Chiefs are third at 9.7%, priced higher on Polymarket (10.1 cents) than on Kalshi (9.5 cents). The Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears are next at about 7.5% each, with the Los Angeles Rams at 6.5%.

The week's movers show how unsettled it is. Seattle climbed from 6% to 8% on Kalshi's daily close and Cincinnati from 4% to 6%, the two biggest gains of the last seven days. Houston fell from 4% to 2%. At the top, San Francisco slipped 1 point on the week while Buffalo gained 1 point — first and second are converging, not separating.

The money is deep even without a leader. On Kalshi alone, the Rams' Super Bowl contract has traded 13,065,216 contracts lifetime, the most of any top-eight team, ahead of San Francisco at 12,353,296 and Chicago at 11,111,112. Polymarket's 32 yes prices sum to 103.4%, a reminder that each team's contract trades in its own order book.

The same disagreement runs through the MVP market: Josh Allen leads at 30.5% on Kalshi and 32% on Polymarket, but on Joe Burrow the books do not even overlap — Kalshi prices him at 17.5% for MVP, Polymarket at 15%, with Kalshi's best bid above Polymarket's best ask. Two crowds, two answers, and a long season left to settle both.

item.description:
Four Days Out: The House Looks Settled, the Senate Does Not

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, and with four days left the prediction markets have split Congress in two. The House looks close to settled: Polymarket prices Democrats at 94% to win it and Kalshi at 92%. The Senate is the real contest, priced at 69% for Democrats on both exchanges.

The combinations tell the same story. Kalshi prices a Democratic sweep of both chambers at 67.5%, a Democratic House with a Republican Senate at 26.5%, and a Republican sweep at just 7.3%. Traders have put $21 million into election markets in the past 24 hours alone, according to DeFi Rate.

The Senate map runs through a handful of races. Democrats need a net gain of four seats, and DeFi Rate notes the 51st seat runs through Maine, where Democrat Troy Jackson is priced at 68%. The biggest move of the last seven days is Kansas, where the Democrat's chance jumped from 40% to 53%.

Texas moved the same way: the Democrat rose from 65% to 72% over the week, while in Alaska the Democrat eased from 76% to 69%. The single most likely Senate outcome is Democrats holding more than 52 seats, at 35%, and the most likely House outcome is 230 to 233 Democratic seats, at 16%.

The polls point the same way, just less far. RealClearPolling's generic congressional ballot average has Democrats ahead 51.4% to 43.2%, an 8.2-point lead. The markets have gone further than the polls. Whether that gap is foresight or enthusiasm is what Tuesday settles.

item.description:
One Exchange Now Handles Three-Quarters of Everything

Prediction markets traded $121.6 billion in contracts in the last 30 days, and one exchange handled almost all of it. DeFi Rate puts Kalshi at $91.7 billion over Sep. 30 to Oct. 29, a 75.6% share, up 53% on the 30 days before. Polymarket US was a distant second at $14.1 billion and 11.6%, with Polymarket's international exchange at $5.0 billion and 4.1%.

The dollars tell a second story. Those $121.6 billion in contracts were $29.2 billion in dollars actually paid, and $4.2 billion traded in the last 24 hours alone. Oct. 29 printed $4.08 billion across all venues and Oct. 28 printed $4.50 billion, while Sunday, Oct. 25 was the busiest day in the window at $7.14 billion — football weekends still set the calendar.

Sports explain the concentration. Sports took 68% of the dollars paid on single markets, $14.8 billion in 30 days, ahead of crypto at 26% and finance at 3%. The single most-traded market in the last 24 hours was Carolina vs. Green Bay on Kalshi at $40 million, followed by Shelton vs. Kym at $19 million.

The challengers are growing faster, just from far behind. DraftKings Predictions and Novig both rose 115% on the prior 30 days, to $4.1 billion and $3.0 billion, and Underdog Exchange was the fastest grower at 158%. September as a whole traded $79.6 billion, up 56% — the question now is whether anyone closes the gap on the leader, or whether scale itself becomes the moat.

item.title: The Market Is Watching Itself: Polymarket's Hunt for Insider Bets — Oct 30, 2026 · 12:10 PM ET
item.description:
The Market Is Watching Itself: Polymarket's Hunt for Insider Bets

Four days before the November 3 midterms, Polymarket is investigating dozens of its own election bets. The platform runs 506 individual election markets, and its compliance team is examining trading that may have used information traders had a duty to protect. At least two cases have already been referred to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

The hunt is led by Shana Bautista, a former FBI official who joined Polymarket in June and now runs a 16-person intelligence and investigations team. Its surveillance system pulls gigabytes of data per user — social media, Federal Election Commission filings, banking partners, cryptocurrency records and statistical models — and processes hundreds of alerts a day. Concentrated trading bursts, multiple accounts behaving alike and shared device identifiers all trigger a closer look, and alerts that cross internal thresholds go straight to Bautista's phone.

The money at stake explains the effort. Combined midterm trading across Polymarket and Kalshi passed $220 million by mid-October. Polymarket's House control market has drawn $24 million with Democrats priced at 92%, its Senate market $9 million with Democrats at 66%, and its balance-of-power contracts price a Democratic sweep at 65% against just 8% for a Republican sweep. Texas leads the Senate battlegrounds at $7 million in volume, with Michigan and Maine at $3 million each.

Polymarket is not alone in policing itself. Kalshi banned and fined political candidates for betting on themselves in April and handed a lifetime ban to former Rep. George Santos in July; it has opened more than 150 investigations this year and sent over 20 cases to law enforcement. Polymarket itself had previously referred more than 100 cases across various markets to law enforcement.

That self-policing now carries the market's credibility. Election prices shape fundraising, media narratives and voter perceptions, so a price moved by private polling is not just a bad trade — it distorts the signal everyone else is reading. Bautista's warning is blunt: if you have information you have a duty to protect, do not trade on it — we will find you.
